timeline.what: Dashboard titled 'Node Foyer' displays status cards for 'NodeRoom', 'NodeSlide', 'parity-studio', and 'NodeVideo'.
Page scrolls down showing registry-only project cards including 'NodeKit', 'NodeMem', and '__fixture_dead'.
View moves back to top cards, highlighting 'VERIFIED' badges on 'NodeRoom' and 'NodeSlide'.
Detail panel opens beneath 'NodeSlide' showing state history and metadata.
Detail panel displays expanded HTTP response status, timestamps, and commit hashes.
View focuses on '__fixture_dead' card displaying an 'UNKNOWN' badge and error message.
View shifts to left panel displaying verification receipt for 'node-foyer' itself.

storyboard_clarity.evidence: 00:00 to 00:21 clearly establishes the problem (trusting status boards), demonstrates verification receipts (00:13), negative testing (00:17), and self-verification (00:21).

state_coverage.evidence: 00:09 shows state transition from collapsed to expanded detail panel, but omits intermediate loading or empty states.

cursor_truth.evidence: 00:06, 00:11, and 00:17 show visible hovers over controls/cards, but 00:09 opens panel without an explicit click ripple/action.

caption_sync.evidence: 00:00 through 00:21 captions precisely match on-screen visuals and male voice narration.

pacing.evidence: Scene transitions occur at 3-4 second intervals (00:00, 00:03, 00:06, 00:09, 00:13, 00:17, 00:21), allowing comfortable reading time.

legibility.evidence: 00:00 text overlays and 00:13 HTTP status, commit hashes, and timestamps are clear and legible.

proof_feel.evidence: 00:13 displays real HTTP responses and commit hashes, while 00:17 shows a deliberately failing fixture card (__fixture_dead) to prove unedited integrity.

safety.evidence: 00:13 displays commit hashes and public status endpoints; no tokens, secrets, or sensitive private data are exposed.

loop_etiquette.evidence: 00:21 to 00:25 ends cleanly following narration, but lacks an explicit hold state or loop transition back to start.

motion_craft.evidence: Camera movements at 00:03 (scroll down), 00:06 (scroll top), 00:17 (card focus), and 00:21 (panel focus) intentionally reveal key evidence.

visual_hierarchy.evidence: 00:06 highlights VERIFIED badges, 00:17 isolates the failing fixture card, and 00:21 shifts focus to the self-checking left panel.

defects.observed: Detail panel expands following hover without showing a click action trigger.
defects.fix: Add a visible cursor click ripple at 00:08 prior to expanding the detail panel.

defects.observed: Video ends on self-check view without a short call-to-action or onboarding step showing how to connect a new repo.
defects.fix: Add a brief closing frame showing how a release lead connects a service or repository.

singleMoment: The highlight of '__fixture_dead' at 00:17 demonstrating an intentionally broken check to prove status results are not faked.
summary: An exemplary, story-first walkthrough that avoids hero-shot traps by showing real receipts, commit hashes, and a negative test fixture. Pacing, caption sync, and narration are well aligned, making the value proposition instantly clear.

persona.evidence: Explicitly addresses 'a release lead who has to trust a status board without reading anyone's source code'.

purpose.evidence: Solves the problem of verifying status board reliability without inspecting underlying repository source code.

use_case.evidence: Auditing health badges, HTTP receipts, and state history across 22 microservice projects.

feature_clarity.evidence: Node Foyer provides verified status badges backed by state history, commit receipts, and self-checks.

full_interaction.evidence: Panel expansion at 00:09 occurs immediately after cursor hover without showing explicit click actuation.

responsiveness.evidence: Panel expands instantaneously with no loading state or latency shown.

flow.evidence: Logical progression from persona intro (00:00), board overview (00:03), receipt inspection (00:13), negative test (00:17), to self-check (00:21).

result.evidence: Displays exact HTTP response codes, commit hashes, and timestamp verification receipts on screen.

non_expert_sense.evidence: Narration translates technical concepts into clear plain English ('Green means verified', 'receipt behind the badge', 'deliberately broken on purpose').

transfer.evidence: Demonstrates product evaluation and self-checking well, but leaves repository setup/onboarding steps implicit.

momLosesThemAt.what: Technical details showing HTTP statuses and commit hashes, though narration maintains high-level context.

cursorEvents.what: Cursor hovers over metadata link under 'NodeSlide'.

textShown.text: For a release lead who has to trust a status board without reading anyone's source code...
Twenty-two products are tracked here, each with its own honest badge...
Green means verified. For this product both the website people see and the service behind it were checked...
This green badge has held state for 23 checks in a row, back to back...
Hovering shows the receipt behind the badge: the exact address it checked...
One product here is deliberately broken on purpose, to prove the checker doesn't fake results...
This board even checks itself — the highlighted card is this board's own card (node-foyer)...

audio.voice: Male voice narration reading the onscreen text overlay.
